title: NSWP arrival context
description: The JSON inside #nswp=<base64url, no padding>. Destinations must read it, then remove it from the URL with history.replaceState before loading third-party scripts. Assertions and receipts are untrusted until verified server-side. See spec §4.4.

signer.description: Where the visitor's signer is: its signer/ and connect/ pages are under this address. Left out, beside the Airlock.

sessionKey.description: The secret half of the session key the pass names. Present only with `pass`.

immersive.description: True when the visitor left a headset session to make this trip.

home.description: True when this world is where the visitor starts, and their own client has brought them home.

joined.description: True when the visitor was in a room where they came from and stays among people here: the world joins its open room without asking again.

mic.description: True when their microphone was on and they have told their client it may stay on as they travel. Read only with joined.

moving.description: How the visitor was moving where they came from. Intense: at a desk, the mouse looks and keys walk; in a headset, they walk and turn smoothly. A world that offers the two ways starts them in this one. Left out means casual.

form.description: What the visitor was using a flat screen with where they came from: their fingers, or a mouse and keys. A world starts them the same way where their device can do both. A preference.

settings.description: The visitor's settings where they came from. A world starts from them. Preferences: a reader keeps what it knows and is in range, and ignores the rest.

text.description: The size of text and controls, 1 being normal.

full.description: They prefer the world filling their screen.

intense.description: They prefer the intense way of moving at a desk.

headset.description: How they prefer to move in a headset: casual (point to step, turn in notches) or intense (walk and turn smoothly). Both are said.

look.description: How fast the view turns under a mouse or a finger, 1 being normal.

fov.description: How wide they see at a desk, top to bottom, in degrees.

pictures.description: Whether they see other people's pictures. A picture is fetched from its owner's own host.

chat.description: Whether they see what other people write in a room, and may write there.

blocked.description: Identity keys of people the visitor has blocked: their own client's list. The world connects them to nobody on it for this visit, and does not keep it.
